## Pen and Paper: Rank the Club Members Before the Lecture

Do this *before* the lecture. It is designed so that you invent the measures
yourself, with nothing but a pencil.

- [Who's the Big Cheese in the University Clubs?](./pen-and-paper/exercise.pdf):
  rank the members of a small club network by hand, four different ways, and
  find out that the four rankings disagree.

## Assignments

### Pair Notebook

Work through this module with the AI tutor and hand in the notebook that the session builds. What is graded is your reasoning, not your code — see [the Pair Notebook guide](../course/pair-notebook.qmd) for the setup and a walkthrough of a full session.

- Repository for M06: coming soon. Your invitation link arrives through Classroom 50.

### Group Mini-Project

Groups of up to three. One repository per group, graded once, with the same score going to every member of the group. Read [how a mini-project runs](../course/mini-project.qmd) first — exactly one person accepts the assignment and invites the rest, and that is the step teams get wrong.

- Repository for M06: [`adv-net-sci-mini-proj-centrality`](https://github.com/sk-classroom/adv-net-sci-mini-proj-centrality). Accept the invitation through Classroom 50 first — the repository is not public, so the link only opens once you are enrolled.

Readers who are not enrolled in SSIE 641 cannot open the assignment repositories. The worksheet above and the [hands-on notebook](02-coding.qmd) cover the same material and need no enrollment.
